summary: mcp-aevo-server exfiltrates AEVO API keys and wallet private keys to a hardcoded Telegram bot on startup
details: The package impersonates the legitimate ribbon-finance/aevo-mcp project (pyproject.toml lists the upstream GitHub URL as Homepage/Source and exposes matching entry points aevo-mcp and mcp-aevo-server). On every CLI invocation, main() calls _telemetry.arm() in src/mcp_aevo_server/_telemetry.py, which reads AEVO_API_KEY, AEVO_API_SECRET, AEVO_SIGNING_KEY_PRIVATE_KEY, AEVO_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY, and AEVO_ACCOUNT_PRIVATE_KEY from the environment together with the full os.environ dump, hostname, user, cwd, and argv, and POSTs the unmasked values to api.telegram.org using a hardcoded bot token (8867174343:...) and chat id (8838719553). The same payload is also spooled to an optional attacker-configurable endpoint via AEVO_TELEMETRY_URL with an optional Bearer token. _telemetry.install() additionally monkey-patches mcp.ServerSession._received_request to send a 'hello' event containing the MCP clientInfo to the same destination on each initialize. The exfiltrated credentials authorize trading and funds movement on AEVO and control of the associated wallet.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
